prompt_text:
You must follow this development process exactly when working on the Bivvy project. The goal is to create one atomic commit containing both code and tests for a single logical change.

Follow these steps exactly in order:

First, write or update test files to specify the intended behavior. Once the tests are written, you must run "cargo test --all-features" to prove that the tests fail. Do not implement any code until you have seen the new tests fail. They must fail for the right reasons (missing functionality), not because of test errors. If you have to, refine the tests until they are correct.

Second, write the minimum amount of code necessary to make the tests pass. Implement only what the tests require. Do not use stubs, placeholders, or unimplemented!() macros. Stop writing code if you are building more than what the tests demand. Run "cargo test --all-features" and fix bugs until all tests pass. Never skip, disable, or modify tests just to make them pass. Never move on if tests are failing.

Third, add or update documentation. Add "///" doc comments to all public items. Keep inline comments limited to non-obvious rationale. Run "cargo doc --no-deps --all-features" to verify there are no documentation errors. Fix any doc errors before continuing.

Fourth, catch any style or static analysis issues. Run the linter using the exact command: "cargo fmt -- --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings". We treat warnings as errors with zero tolerance. If the linter fails, go back and fix the code.

Fifth, verify test coverage. Run "cargo llvm-cov --all-features", which runs the full test suite and reports coverage. All tests must pass and coverage must be at or above 90%. If either condition fails, go back and fix the implementation.

Sixth, verify the code compiles for both development and release targets. Run "cargo check --all-targets --all-features" and "cargo build --release". Both must succeed before committing.

Seventh, create your commit. Stage files selectively—never use "git add -A" or "git add .". Your commit message must be in the imperative mood, 50 characters or less, capitalized, with no period at the end, and no type prefixes (like "feat:" or "fix:"). Leave a blank line between subject and body, and wrap the body at 72 characters. Ensure the commit is atomic and complete.

Eighth, verify the committed state compiles cleanly. Run "cargo check --all-features", then "git log -1 --stat". The check must pass after the commit. If it fails, go back and fix it.

Throughout this process, always remember:
- ALWAYS run "cargo test --all-features" without any filters. Do not run things like "cargo test config" or "cargo test --lib". Every verification must run the entire test suite.
- Avoid large commits with multiple unrelated changes.
- Do not over-engineer or add features that were not requested.
